item.content:encoded:
It was never their wheel in the first place — if they want to use it, more power to them, but that means dealing with the consequences of using a wheel designed by someone else for an entirely different vehicle — so don't be surprised if there are some bumps.

That said, tt's not that hard to make a CSS theme, and the CC nature of the site means that you could even just copy the Unusual Investigations theme in its entirety.

item.title: (no title)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This article uses a CSS theme that I made for a specific tale series, and which was never intended for use outside of said series — because it was made solely for my own use, I disabled the translation module due to its incompatibility with CSS stylings. This was a personal decision made on my part in the interest of aesthetics and immersion, and was never meant to affect any articles other than my own — if the author insists on continuing to use this theme, then that is their prerogative and there is very little I can do to stop them, although it was not made with the expectation that others would use it, and I would prefer if they didn't.

Edit: I've gone ahead and move the theme url (breaking any links to it) and re-titled the page to better reflect that it is a tale-series specific theme. Please stop adding it to UIU goi formats.
